item.title: Bus passengers face HK$5,000 fine, 3-month jail for not wearing seat belts from Jan 25
item.description: Hong Kong will tighten its road safety regulations on January 25, with passengers who fail to wear seat belts on public transport and commercial vehicles facing fines of up to HK$5,000 and three months in prison. item.title: Hong Kong public hospital A&E visits drop following doubling of fees for low-priority cases
item.description: The number of patients visiting the Accident and Emergency Departments (A&E) at Hong Kong’s public hospitals has dropped after authorities more than doubled the fees from HK$180 to HK$400 for low-priority cases in a bid to curb misuse. item.title: China consumer prices rise at fastest pace since 2023
item.description: Chinese consumer prices rose last month at their fastest pace in nearly three years, official data showed Friday, extending a period of growth following months of deflationary pressure in the world’s second-largest economy. The consumer price index (CPI), a key measure of inflation, rose 0.8 percent year-on-year in December, the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) […]

item.title: Hong Kong legal reform body suggests new cybercrime law with up to life imprisonment for systems interference
item.description: Hong Kong’s law reform body has suggested introducing new cybercrime legislation to target five types of offences, including illegal interference with computer systems and data, which it said should warrant a maximum sentence of life imprisonment in life-threatening cases. item.title: China: the indispensable partner of Maduro’s Venezuela
item.description: China was the dominant buyer of Venezuelan oil under deposed president Nicolas Maduro, the fulcrum of a symbiotic partnership that propped up the South American economy and gave Beijing regional influence. item.title: Tai Po fire: Gov’t proposes 9 rehousing plans; on-site redevelopment of Wang Fuk Court may take a decade
item.description: The Hong Kong government has proposed nine rehousing plans for homeowners of Tai Po’s fire-hit Wang Fuk Court, ranging from an option allowing relocation as early as September to an on-site redevelopment that may take a decade. item.description: A college student union at the Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) has disbanded, following a string of suspensions of three other college unions last month. item.description: Welcome back to HKFP Monitor. item.title: Slow-motion justice: Not just for political cases nor only a problem for defendants
item.description: Long delays in bringing criminal cases to court have been an unlovely feature of the Hong Kong legal system for a long time. item.title: Scam tycoons making fortunes in Southeast Asia now in China’s crosshairs
item.description: China is moving against the cyberscam tycoons making fortunes in Southeast Asia, driven by mounting public pressure and Beijing’s desire to keep control of judicial processes, analysts say.
